title: Repairing Damage: Pitch Mark on the Fringe
question: Andrew’s ball lies on the putting green. There is a pitch mark on his intended line of play, but the pitch mark itself is on the fringe. May Andrew repair the pitch mark?

choices.text: Yes, because his ball is on the putting green.
No, because the pitch mark is not on the putting green.
Yes, provided it was made by another player’s ball.

explanation: A player may only repair ball marks and other types of damage on the putting green. Andrew is not allowed to repair a pitch mark on the fringe, even if it is on his line of play, because that area is not defined as putting green under the Rules.
imagePrompt: Create a polished, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic and 25% stylised) illustration in an established junior golf quiz style. Show a golfer on a green with his ball clearly on the putting green. Depict a visible pitch mark on the fringe between his ball and the hole in his line of play. The scene should be in daylight on a lush, modern course. The hole should be visible beyond the pitch mark. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer's ball lies on the putting green, with a visible pitch mark on the fringe between the ball and the hole on the player's intended line of play.

sceneSpec.setting: A well-kept golf green and surrounding fringe on a modern course in daylight.
sceneSpec.players: One male golfer (Andrew), dressed in standard golf attire.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Andrew's ball is clearly lying on the putting green.

sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Distinguishing what can and cannot be repaired based on the ball’s location and where the damage is.

Andrew’s ball on the putting green.
The hole visible beyond the pitch mark.
